one_line.text: Israeli historian trained in world, medieval and military history who became a prominent writer of species-scale history and technology books.

biography.text: Born in Israel in 1976, Harari completed a doctorate at Oxford in 2002 and teaches history at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. After Sapiens, he wrote Homo Deus, 21 Lessons for the 21st Century and Nexus, alongside graphic and children's adaptations. He and Itzik Yahav co-founded the education and storytelling company Sapienship in 2019.

background.text: His original academic fields were world, medieval and military history. His later work asks macrohistorical questions about biology, human difference, justice, happiness and technology. The method is synthesis: combine research from many fields into a simple narrative built around large questions and memorable reversals.

expertise.text: Harari has formal expertise in history, especially medieval and military history, and a strong demonstrated skill in explaining macrohistory to general readers. Claims about archaeology, biology, neuroscience and economics extend beyond that training and need support from specialists in those fields.

perspective_and_limits.text: Harari favours distant, species-level explanations and writes for clarity and provocation. That perspective reveals connections across long periods, but can flatten political agency, local variation and expert disagreement. Reviews and specialist critics repeatedly identify the same risk: a persuasive narrative voice can make interpretation sound like settled evidence.
